name: IEEE Ethically Aligned Design (EAD1e, 2019)
organization: IEEE Global Initiative on Ethics of Autonomous and Intelligent Systems
dinh_nghia: IEEE Ethically Aligned Design (EAD), First Edition (EAD1e, 2019), is the IEEE Global Initiative on Ethics of Autonomous and Intelligent Systems' comprehensive framework for aligning AI and autonomous systems with human values. Published by the IEEE Standards Association after four years of development (2016-2019) involving 500+ contributors from over 100 countries, EAD1e is one of the most technically detailed AI ethics documents produced before the EU AI Act. It provides both high-level ethical principles and concrete technical recommendations for AI system designers, engineers, and organizations. For educational AI and academic integrity, EAD1e's principles of Transparency, Accountability, and Awareness of Misuse are most directly relevant.
phan_loai: EAD1e organizes AI ethics obligations under eight General Principles. For academic integrity contexts, the most relevant are: (1) Transparency — AI systems used in educational assessment must be transparent in their operation and decision-making; (2) Accountability — clear human accountability for AI system outcomes; (3) Awareness of Misuse — AI designers must consider how their systems could be misused, including for academic fraud; (4) Data Agency — students have rights over data collected about them by educational AI; (5) Human Well-being — AI systems should enhance, not undermine, human flourishing and genuine learning. Violations include: deploying opaque AI assessment systems; failing to audit AI systems for misuse potential; neglecting data rights of students.
lich_su_khai_niem: The IEEE Global Initiative was launched in 2016 as a response to growing concerns about AI safety and ethics. EAD was developed through three draft versions (v1: 2016, v2: 2017) before the First Edition (EAD1e) was released in 2019. The development process was unusual for IEEE in being open, consultative, and multi-disciplinary rather than purely technical. EAD1e was accompanied by draft IEEE standards including P7000 (Model Process for Addressing Ethical Concerns), P7001 (Transparency of Autonomous Systems), and P7002 (Data Privacy Process). The framework influenced subsequent AI ethics documents including the EU AI Act and UNESCO 2021 Recommendation.
ten_truong_hop: EAD1e has been applied in: (1) IEEE member companies developing educational AI (e.g., IBM Watson Education, Microsoft Azure AI in Education); (2) Government AI ethics frameworks in Australia, Canada, and Singapore that reference IEEE standards; (3) University AI ethics programs that use EAD1e as a teaching document; (4) EdTech industry self-regulation efforts citing IEEE principles. The Transparency principle (and its derived standard IEEE P7001) has been applied to AI-based student assessment systems in several European universities.
dien_bien: EAD1e's development: IEEE formed the Global Initiative in 2016; 13 committees (General Principles, Embedding Values into Autonomous AI, Methodologies, Data, Legal, Economics, Well-being, Education, Mixed Reality, Policy, Military, News/Entertainment, Medically-enabled AI) produced reports that were integrated into EAD1e. The Education committee specifically addressed AI in education — making EAD1e one of the few major AI ethics documents to include education-specific guidance from a technical professional society perspective. The document was released free of charge to maximize impact.
ket_qua_xu_ly: EAD1e has influenced: (1) IEEE P7000-series standards development (several standards now published); (2) ACM/IEEE joint software engineering ethics work; (3) EU AI Act's risk classification approach (EAD1e's risk-based thinking influenced EU policy); (4) National AI strategies in 50+ countries; (5) Corporate AI ethics frameworks at Google, Microsoft, IBM, and Amazon all reference or align with EAD principles. In education specifically, IEEE published a companion 'AI in Education' report (2019) that applies EAD principles to educational contexts.
con_so_thong_ke: Development: 2016-2019; 4 years; 500+ contributors; 100+ countries represented; 294 pages (EAD1e); 8 general principles; 10+ draft standards generated (P7000 series); free download; IEEE membership 420,000 in 160+ countries; EAD1e available in English (translations limited) [uncertain: translation status]; cited in EU AI Act development process.
hai_cho_nguoi_hoc: EAD1e's Human Well-being principle explicitly prioritizes genuine human flourishing over narrow metrics: an AI educational system that optimizes test scores while undermining genuine learning (by enabling AI-assisted fraud) violates the Human Well-being principle. The Data Agency principle protects students' rights over data collected about them by educational AI — including exam proctoring data, AI tutoring interaction logs, and behavioral analytics. EAD1e requires that AI systems be designed to enhance human capability, not create dependency — directly addressing the risk of over-reliance on AI writing tools.
hai_cho_nghien_cuu: EAD1e's Transparency principle directly addresses research integrity: AI systems involved in research (literature review, data analysis, manuscript generation) must be transparent about their operation. The Accountability principle requires identifiable human accountability for AI-assisted research outputs — if an AI system generates a hallucinated citation, the researcher (not the AI) is accountable for verifying it. EAD1e's Data Agency principle applies to AI systems trained on scientific papers — the rights of original authors over their data in AI training sets.
hai_cho_xa_hoi: The Human Well-being principle frames AI's societal impact in terms of genuine human flourishing, not just immediate user satisfaction. AI academic fraud that allows students to obtain degrees without genuine competency harms not only the educational institution but the professionals, patients, clients, and communities who will be served by incompetent credentialed graduates. EAD1e explicitly addresses societal-level harm from AI systems that optimize local metrics (student grades) at the expense of broader values (genuine education).
cong_cu_phat_hien: The Transparency principle (and its associated IEEE P7001 standard on Transparency of Autonomous Systems) directly applies to AI detection tools: (1) AI detectors used in academic integrity proceedings must be transparent about their operation; (2) Affected students have a right to understand how the AI detector made its determination; (3) The Accountability principle requires identifiable human accountability for false positive accusations generated by AI detectors; (4) The Awareness of Misuse principle requires that AI detector designers consider how detectors can be gamed (humanization tools, paraphrasing) and design mitigations.
han_che_cong_cu: EAD1e's Data Agency principle is particularly relevant to AI detection bias: students provide their writing to AI detectors, which constitutes data collection. Under Data Agency, students should have rights over how their writing data is used, stored, and processed. The Liang et al. (Stanford, 2023) ESL bias finding creates an accountability problem under EAD1e: the organizations that deployed biased detectors must be held accountable for false positive harms under the Accountability principle.
watermarking: IEEE P7001 (Transparency of Autonomous Systems, published 2021) provides technical standards for AI system transparency that apply to watermarking: watermarking schemes must be transparent to affected parties about what information is embedded, who can read it, and how it will be used. EAD1e's Data Agency principle raises privacy concerns about watermarking: if watermarks can de-anonymize student writing, they may infringe on student data rights. The Awareness of Misuse principle requires watermarking researchers to address watermark stripping attacks in their design.
thiet_ke_bai_tap: EAD1e's Human Well-being and Accountability principles motivate assessment designs that verify genuine human capability: assessments where AI can invisibly complete all the work violate the Educational purpose that assessments serve (Human Well-being). The Accountability principle applied to assessment design: when AI completes an assessment, who is accountable for the learning outcome? Accountability requires that assessments be designed so that human learners bear genuine accountability for their performance — motivating process-based, oral, and portfolio assessments.
chinh_sach_truong_hoc: EAD1e's Accountability principle requires institutions to establish clear governance for educational AI deployment: who is responsible when an AI admission system makes a biased decision? When an AI grading system makes an error? When an AI proctor wrongly flags a student? The principle requires institutional policies to specify accountability chains for all educational AI applications — a governance design requirement that most university AI policies currently do not meet.
van_hoa_to_chuc: EAD1e explicitly addresses organizational culture: Chapter 3 (Accountability) discusses the role of organizational culture in ensuring that engineering ethics is not merely procedural but embedded in professional identity. This aligns with McCabe's honor culture research and Bretag's Approach element: the most effective integrity cultures are those where values are internalized, not just enforced. EAD1e requires AI development organizations to build ethical AI culture through hiring, training, and incentive alignment.
ai_literacy: EAD1e's awareness of misuse principle requires AI practitioners to understand how AI can be misused — this is a professional AI literacy competency that parallels the student/faculty AI literacy required by UNESCO 2023 and EU AI Act Article 4. The Education chapter of EAD1e specifically addresses AI literacy in education systems — recommending that educational institutions teach AI ethics alongside AI technical skills. EAD1e provides the engineering professional perspective on AI literacy that complements UNESCO's educational perspective.
khung_quoc_te: EAD1e is the primary technical professional society contribution to AI ethics, complementing: UNESCO 2021 (intergovernmental), EU AI Act (legislative), ACM Code (computing professionals). IEEE EAD and ACM Code together cover professional obligations of engineers and computing practitioners. EAD1e's Transparency principle is operationalized by EU AI Act Article 50; its Accountability principle by EU AI Act's human oversight requirements; its Data Agency principle by EU AI Act's data governance requirements. The convergence of these frameworks reflects an emerging international consensus on AI ethics.
phap_luat_viet_nam: IEEE has a Vietnam Section (IEEE Vietnam Section) with thousands of members in engineering and technology fields. Vietnamese IEEE members — particularly those working in EdTech, AI, and computing — have professional obligations under EAD1e's principles. Vietnam's Law on Science and Technology (2025) references international standards; IEEE standards (including P7001 Transparency) are potential technical references for Vietnam's AI governance. The Awareness of Misuse principle is directly applicable to Vietnamese EdTech developers building AI tools used in educational assessment.
chinh_sach_chau_a: IEEE has the largest Asian membership of any technology professional society. EAD1e principles are increasingly influential in Asian AI governance: Singapore's AI Governance Framework references IEEE standards; Japan's Society 5.0 AI ethics framework aligns with EAD principles; South Korea's AI ethics guidelines reference IEEE EAD; India's Responsible AI Framework references IEEE standards. In higher education, IEEE-affiliated engineering schools in Asia (IITs, NUS Engineering, HCMUT) are natural venues for EAD1e adoption.
ai_tutor_vs_ai_cheater: EAD1e's Human Well-being principle provides the most precise technical ethics answer to the tutor/cheater debate: AI functions as a tutor when it demonstrably enhances human learning (measurable improvement in genuine competency) and as a cheater when it displaces human learning (no competency development despite credential acquisition). The Accountability principle ensures that the student, not the AI, remains accountable for learning outcomes — regardless of AI assistance level. The Awareness of Misuse principle obligates AI tool designers to consider and mitigate the cheating use case.
edtech_company_policies: EAD1e's five principles create design obligations for EdTech companies: (1) Transparency — EdTech AI must explain its operations to students and teachers; (2) Accountability — clear responsibility chains for AI-generated educational decisions; (3) Human Well-being — EdTech AI must demonstrably enhance, not harm, learning outcomes; (4) Data Agency — students must have meaningful control over their educational data; (5) Awareness of Misuse — EdTech companies must assess and mitigate AI misuse for academic fraud. Current EdTech company policies vary widely in meeting these obligations; Khan Academy Khanmigo's design most comprehensively satisfies EAD1e principles among major platforms.
de_xuat_nha_nghien_cuu: Applying EAD1e to EdTech AI integrity research: (1) Use the Transparency principle to develop an audit instrument for AI systems used in Vietnamese university assessment — requiring technical documentation meeting IEEE P7001 standards; (2) Apply the Accountability principle to map responsibility chains in Vietnamese EdTech deployments — who is accountable when an AI admission or assessment system makes a harmful error?; (3) Use the Awareness of Misuse principle to require that Vietnamese EdTech developers conduct misuse risk assessments before deploying educational AI; (4) Apply Data Agency principles to analyze Vietnamese university EdTech data governance — do students have meaningful rights over data collected about them?; (5) Propose that Vietnam's VAIP (computing professional association) and IEEE Vietnam Section jointly develop an EAD1e-aligned code of conduct for Vietnamese EdTech practitioners.

Vietnamese IEEE members working in AI and EdTech are professionally bound by EAD1e principles. The IEEE Vietnam Section has hosted events on AI ethics [uncertain: specific EAD1e-focused events].
